question: In Young’s double-slit experiment, light shows interference, while in the photoelectric effect, light ejects electrons from a metal surface. Explain how these two observations show different aspects of the nature of light.

options.A: Interference demonstrates the particle aspect, whereas the photoelectric effect supports the longitudinal wave aspect.
options.B: Both experiments provide exclusive evidence that light consists solely of classical continuous waves.
options.C: Interference is a ray optics phenomenon, while the photoelectric effect is explained by gravitational attraction.
options.D: Interference shows the wave nature of light through superposition, while the photoelectric effect supports the particle nature of light through photon-electron interactions.
